items.q: Do I need a design before contacting you?
items.a: No. Tell us what you want to change, and share drawings or inspiration if you have them.

items.q: Can I keep the existing layout?
items.a: Yes. If the layout already works, the project can focus on cabinetry, surfaces, fixtures and finishes.

items.q: What affects the cost?
items.a: The size and condition of the room, layout changes, cabinetry, appliances and finishes. We prepare an estimate once the scope is defined.

link.text: Prefer to spread the cost? See financing options.

items.q: How long will the renovation take?
items.a: It depends on the scope, permits, your selections and how long materials take to arrive. If you have a date to work to, like a holiday or a move, tell us at the start.

items.q: My house is older. Does lead paint matter?
items.a: If it was built before 1978, it may have lead paint. We plan containment, dust control and clean-up into the scope from the first visit.

items.q: Can you work on a small bathroom?
items.a: Yes. We welcome smaller bathroom projects as well as larger renovations.

items.q: Can the bathroom layout change?
items.a: Often. It depends on the building, the plumbing and the space available. Share your goals and we will review the options.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom easier to use as we get older?
items.a: Yes. Tell us who uses the room and what’s hard today, like the step into the shower, the door, or somewhere to hold on, and we’ll plan the room around it.

items.q: Can a bathroom be part of a whole-home renovation?
items.a: Yes. Planning it with the other rooms keeps the work and the decisions coordinated.

items.q: My house is older. Does lead paint matter?
items.a: If it was built before 1978, it may have lead paint. We plan containment, dust control and clean-up into the scope from the first visit.

items.q: Does the entire house have to be renovated at once?
items.a: No. We’ll tell you which parts make sense to do together and which can wait.

items.q: Can I live at home during the work?

items.q: Our house is older. What about lead paint?

items.q: Can you tell me whether an addition is possible from a message?

items.q: Do additions require permits?

items.q: Can an addition include remodeling existing rooms?
items.a: Yes. Tell us about the new space and the rooms you want to change, and we will plan them together.

title: Roof Repair & Replacement in DC | I.S Design + Build
description: Discuss roof repairs, replacement and associated concerns with I.S Design + Build. Serving Washington, DC, Northern Virginia and Montgomery County.
label: Roofing
headline: Roof repair and replacement.
lede: Leaks, storm damage or a worn-out roof. Call now; out of office hours, leave your address and number and we’ll call you back. We tell you whether to repair or replace, and we fix the damage inside too.

sections.label: What we do
sections.title: Repair it or replace it. We’ll tell you which.

items.name: Roof repairs
items.text: Leaks, visible wear or one problem area.

items.name: Roof replacement
items.text: A new roof in materials that suit the property.

items.name: Water damage
items.text: We repair the stained ceiling and walls along with the roof, so you deal with one company.

sections.label: When you get in touch
sections.title: Tell us what you’re seeing.
text: Where the property is and whether water is coming in. Photos from the ground help. Please don’t climb onto the roof.
Until we get there: move belongings away from the drip and catch it in a bucket, keep clear of a sagging ceiling and of light fittings with water in them, and take photos for your insurer.

items.q: How do I know whether to repair or replace the roof?
items.a: It depends on the roof’s condition and the extent of the damage. We assess the roof before recommending either.

items.q: Can I send photographs?
items.a: Yes. Email them to contact@isdesignandbuild.com, or send them in the chat. Use photographs you can take safely from the ground.

items.q: What if water is coming in now?
items.a: Call (202) 519-1831 and say water is coming in. We’ll tell you on the call how soon we can get there. Outside office hours, leave a message with your address and phone number.

title: DC Remodeling & Roofing Questions | I.S Design + Build
description: Straight answers about licences, permits, lead paint, cost, living at home during the work and service areas, from a DC remodeling and roofing firm.
label: FAQs
headline: Straight answers before you start.
lede: Planning a room, a roof or a larger renovation? Start here.

items.q: What services do you offer?
items.a: Kitchen and bathroom remodeling, whole-home renovations, home additions, roofing and lead-paint work. If your project includes something else, tell us about it when you call or chat.

items.q: Do you take smaller projects?
items.a: Yes. We welcome single-room projects as well as substantial renovations.

items.q: Where do you work?
items.a: Washington, DC, Northern Virginia and Montgomery County, Maryland, including Bethesda and Chevy Chase. Share your town to confirm coverage.

items.q: Are you licensed and insured?
items.a: Ask us for our licence numbers and certificate of insurance when we first talk, and check them before you sign with any contractor.

items.q: Do you handle permits?
items.a: Yes. We find out which approvals your project needs and handle the applications before work starts.

items.q: Can I live at home during the work?
items.a: It depends on which rooms are affected and whether you’ll be without a kitchen, a bathroom, water or power for a time. We plan the order of work with you, so you know before we start.

items.q: My house was built before 1978. Does lead paint matter?
items.a: It may have lead paint. We plan containment, dust control and clean-up into the scope from the first visit.

items.q: Can you work with my architect or designer?
items.a: Yes. An independent interior designer who worked alongside us on a new four-storey home is among our Google reviewers.

items.q: Do I need drawings before contacting you?
items.a: No. A description of what you want to change is enough. Include drawings or photographs if you have them.

items.q: Can you give me a price online?
items.a: Not an accurate one, because every house is different. Tell us what you want to change and, if you have one, a budget range. We’ll talk it through and prepare an estimate once we’ve seen the house.

items.q: I live out of town. Can you run my project?
items.a: Yes. Clients living abroad have run their projects with us, with regular updates and every decision agreed with them.

items.q: Do you take commercial and government work?
items.a: Yes. Call (202) 519-1831 to talk about the property and the work.

items.q: How do I speak to someone?
items.a: Call (202) 519-1831, Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, or email contact@isdesignandbuild.com. Outside those hours, use Chat now: Tony, our AI assistant, answers at any time and passes your details to our team.

items.q: Do I have to use financing?
items.a: No. It is one way to pay. We discuss payment when the scope and estimate are prepared.

items.q: How are rates and payments set?
items.a: By the lender, based on the loan and your circumstances. Read the lender’s terms before you commit, and compare more than one offer.

items.q: Does applying commit me to a project?
items.a: No. Applying to a lender is separate from agreeing a project with us. Ask the lender how an application affects you.

items.q: Can I finance roofing work?
items.a: Ask the lender whether the work qualifies. Eligibility is the lender’s decision.

title: Lead Paint & Lead-Safe Renovation in DC | I.S Design + Build
description: Lead-safe renovation for DC homes and rentals built before 1978: containment, dust control, clean-up and clearance testing planned from the first visit.
label: Lead paint
headline: Lead-safe work for older DC homes and rentals.
lede: For homes and rentals built before 1978. We plan containment, dust control and clean-up into the scope from the first visit, and arrange the clearance testing at the end.

sections.label: Why it matters
sections.title: Old paint becomes dust.
text: Sanding, cutting and demolition release it. Lead dust is harmful, especially to young children and during pregnancy. The EPA sets rules for renovation work in pre-1978 homes.

link.text: Read the EPA’s guidance on lead

sections.label: What to tell us
sections.title: Raise it at the start.

items.name: The home
items.text: Its age, and any inspection or risk-assessment reports you have.

items.name: The work
items.text: Which rooms and surfaces are affected, and whether paint is peeling.

items.name: The household
items.text: Young children or anyone pregnant living in the home.

sections.note: Lead inspections and risk assessments are carried out by a licensed inspector or risk assessor.

sections.label: Landlords
sections.title: Renting it out?
text: Tell us if you have a DOEE notice or order, a risk-assessment report, or a date the unit must be ready, and we’ll plan the work around it.

items.q: How do I know whether my home has lead paint?
items.a: The age of the home is the first sign. Only testing by a qualified professional can confirm it. Do not sand or scrape paint to find out.

items.q: Can I stay at home during the work?
items.a: It depends on the areas affected and how they can be separated from the rest of the home. We discuss it before work is scheduled.

items.q: Is this a separate project?
items.a: It can be part of a renovation or a request on its own. Tell us what you need when you call or chat.
